identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection record for one forklift (Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2, propane) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026, showing 19 shift inspections with 12 checklist items per day. The log is required under 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) and tracks daily pre-shift safety checks by two operators; the company must remove any truck from service if an inspection reveals a defect affecting safety.
scan.freshness_note: Log current as of 25 September 2026 (today). The last recorded inspection is 19 September. No supervisor review date has been filled in yet. Gaps in daily entries (missing Sep 3, 4, 6, 7, 13, 14) are explained by the hour meter rising on those dates—the truck was in use but inspections were not logged.

gaps.title: Missing inspections on Sep 3–4, 6–7, 13–14
gaps.description: The log shows no entries for Sep 3, 4, 6, 7, 13, or 14. The hour meter on the truck rose on those dates (e.g., from 4,819 at Sep 2 to 4,834 at Sep 5), proving the truck was operated. 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires examination before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety. An inspection is missing for each of these six shifts.
gaps.fix: Complete the missing inspection entries for Sep 3, 4, 6, 7, 13, and 14 or document why they cannot be filled in retroactively. If the truck was used without inspection, that is a violation; if it was idle, the hour meter discrepancy must be resolved. A note should clarify.
gaps.locator: page 1, table; hour meter values, page 1 and 2
gaps.quote: examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety

gaps.title: No action taken after horn defect on Sep 9
gaps.description: On Sep 9, operator M.C. marked the horn with an X and noted "Horn not working." The defect was not corrected; the same operator (M.C.) used the truck again on Sep 10 with a check mark for the horn, and the truck continued in use through Sep 19. 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires that a truck not be placed in service if the examination shows a condition adversely affecting safety, and all defects must be reported and corrected immediately.
gaps.fix: Document what action was taken on Sep 9. Either: (1) the horn was repaired before Sep 10 use, or (2) the truck should not have been placed in service on Sep 10. Add a note showing the date the repair was made and who confirmed it. If no repair occurred, this is a violation.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7); NIOSH guidance: all defects must be reported immediately and corrected before the vehicle can return to service

gaps.title: Supervisor review incomplete
gaps.description: The log includes a signature block for supervisor review with blank lines for name and date. No supervisor has signed off on or reviewed the log entries as of 25 September 2026.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review the log, verify the entries, sign the document, and enter the date. This should happen regularly (weekly or monthly, depending on company policy) to ensure the inspections are being conducted and recorded correctly.

gaps.title: No operator certification dates or evaluation renewal deadlines shown in summary
gaps.description: The log lists two operators: M.C. (certified 2024-03-11, evaluation due 2027-03-11) and J.R. (certified 2025-06-02, evaluation due 2028-06-02). The document does not indicate whether these certifications are current or if the company has a system to track when re-evaluations are due. M.C.'s evaluation is due in about six months (March 2027); J.R.'s is due in about 20 months (June 2028).
gaps.fix: Track operator certifications separately from the inspection log. Maintain a roster showing each operator's name, original certification date, type(s) of truck certified on, and evaluation due date. Ensure re-training and re-evaluation occur before each operator's certification expires. 29 CFR 1910.178(l)(3) requires that evaluations be done at least once every three years.
